NATIVE RATE INFORMATION AND RARE LIFETIMES UNDER MODEL ERROR
Root construction, continued 1 November 2026

Objective retained
==================
Predict a rare coarse-target mean lifetime and its deadline probabilities from
acquired local information, without waiting for the target event. This note
removes an exact-model restriction of the previous construction. The native
process need not have the fitted Gibbs law, preserve a known measure, or have
a supplied stationary short-cycle decomposition. It must have a justified,
bounded kinetic dependence range and the same transition support as a usable
reference. Complete native state changes and calibrated timestamps are inputs.

This is a finite theorem and an executable mathematical construction, not a
physical validation or a claim of historical priority. Count/exposure learning,
hypercontractivity, Markov potential theory and matrix perturbation are ordinary
ingredients. The addition developed here is their explicit composition into a
compact, target-uniform relative lifetime certificate for a misspecified source.
The new interface is stronger than the previous clamped/marked calibration.

All prior Astra premises are bound to
  harjassand/astra-research-knowledge
  51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056.
The previous proofs and source copies in this package remain unmodified.

1. Reference and actual source
=============================
Use finite row generators Q0 and Q, with L0=-Q0 and L=-Q. Both are irreducible.
The reference Q0 is executable, has known stationary probability pi0, a paid
maximum exit bound Lambda, and a paid symmetric Poincare gap g>0:
  E0(f)=<f,L0 f>_pi0 >= g Var_pi0(f).
The actual stationary probability pi is NOT an input. Suppose that native rate
confidence intervals imply the simultaneous edge bounds
  (1-eta) q0_xy <= q_xy <= (1+eta) q0_xy,       x!=y,        (1)
where 0<eta<1, and that both sources have the same off-diagonal support.
The statement is deterministic on this acquisition event.

One also needs a reference relative mixing time r_beta, 0<beta<1, satisfying
  |P0(t)(x,y)/pi0(y)-1| <= beta       for all x,y, t>=r_beta. (2)
Section 5 earns r_beta from compact source structure. An oracle giving (2) is
not assumed in the explicit cube construction.

For every nonempty proper target A, B=A^c, define
  p0=pi0(A), b0=1-p0, p=pi(A), b=1-p,
  M0=E_pi0(.|B) tau_A under Q0,

# Audit: local rate admission, unknown stationary law, and rare means

Parent `/root` owns the rate-admission construction and synthesis. This
note independently checks its algebra, supplies a symmetric flow-error
sharpening, and records an ordinary hypercontractive improvement. It is
not a claim that these ingredients, or their conjunction, are historically
new. Prior Astra premises remain pinned to revision
51ce47ce39f976517d60e2f87bbe280b651f6056.

## 1. Contract and finite-time positive comparison

Let Q0 be an irreducible finite-state generator, with invariant law pi0,
additive symmetric-part gap at least g>0, and exit rates at most Lambda.
Let Q be any generator on the same allowed off-diagonal support satisfying

    (1-eta) q0(x,y) <= q(x,y) <= (1+eta) q0(x,y),  0<=eta<1.

No stationarity, Gibbs representation, cycle decomposition, or reversibility
of Q is assumed. Finite-state irreducibility follows from shared support.
The support and local contexts must be supplied structural information;
finite passive data alone cannot exclude arbitrary hidden transitions or
global-state dependence.

Entrywise comparison of Metzler generators gives

    (1-eta)Q0-2eta Lambda I <= Q <= (1+eta)Q0+2eta Lambda I.

Therefore, by positivity of matrix exponentials,

    exp(-2eta Lambda t) P0((1-eta)t)
       <= P(t) <=
    exp(2eta Lambda t) P0((1+eta)t).                 (1)

The factor2 is sufficient: the diagonal difference between Q and
(1-eta)Q0 can be as negative as -2eta times the reference exit rate.

Suppose the reference admits a certified relative mixing time r_beta:

    |P0(s;x,y)/pi0(y)-1| <= beta  for all s>=r_beta,  0<beta<1.

It suffices to establish this at r_beta, since subsequent Markov averaging
preserves both entrywise bounds. Set

    t_beta = r_beta/(1-eta),
    u = 2eta Lambda t_beta - log(1-beta).

Multiplying (1) by the unknown invariant row law pi and summing over the
initial state proves the pointwise stationary certificate

    exp(-u) pi0(x) <= pi(x) <= exp(u) pi0(x).         (2)

The upper bound uses log(1+beta)<=-log(1-beta). This step requires no
computation or sampling from the true pi. A gap-only reference certificate
is r_beta=log[1/(beta pi0_min)]/g. Section4 greatly improves it for the cube.

## 2. All-target mean comparison by balanced flows

Use L=-Q, D=diag(pi)L and D0=diag(pi0)L0. Both D and D0 have zero row
and column sums. T
